_note: OUR mapping from benchmark names as papers write them to where the artifact lives. Authored, like DOMAIN_FAMILIES: the names are data-derived (the extracted `datasets` field), the locations are ours and are marked as such in the interface. Every hf/gh id is checked against the Hub / GitHub API by `python3 -m icml.resources --registry`; an id that fails the check carries ok:false and shows no link. Matching is by taxonomy.dataset_key over name + aliases. not_a_dataset lists model names the extractor files under datasets; they never become benchmark chips with links. `id` is the benchmark's stable key (owner, 2026-10-02): a slug of its published name, assigned once and never reused. A benchmark is its published product name: aliases are spelling variants or forms the benchmark itself publishes; a differently named product (a subset, a version, a year) is its own entry, and a bare name is left unmapped so it is counted as written. Entries split out on 2026-10-02 carry no location yet. `ambiguous: true` marks a name that is also an ordinary word, a method or an institution (CLEAR, FLAIR, BAIR): it counts only in its registered casing and only where the paper states a role for it.

alias_sources.hendrycks math: EleutherAI lm-evaluation-harness names the MATH task `hendrycks_math` and the Hub copy is EleutherAI/hendrycks_math; both cite Hendrycks et al. (2021). Not to be confused with `minerva_math` (a prompting protocol over MATH) or Minerva Math (separate OCW-course problems).

benchmarks.name: Minerva Math
benchmarks.note: Ambiguous name, kept as written and never linked by name alone: in papers it denotes either OCWCourses (272 university STEM problems from the Minerva paper, Lewkowycz et al. 2022) or lm-evaluation-harness `minerva_math` (MATH under Minerva's prompting and answer checking). Which one needs the cited paper, the problem count or the run settings.

benchmarks.name: ImageNet 128x128

setting.preprocessing: center crop and resize of ImageNet-1k images; the exact protocol is the paper's (e.g. ADM / guided-diffusion)

benchmarks.note: Separate from ImageNet-1k (owner, 2026-10-06): image-generation papers compare results only within one resolution, and the reference code ships per-resolution evaluation batches (guided-diffusion evaluations/README.md; DiT calls ImageNet 256x256 and 512x512 benchmarks). Same images as ImageNet-1k — the relation is recorded, never a merged count.
